claims: "Integrity" is the name given by the Artemis II crew to their Orion spacecraft.
The Orion spacecraft safely splashed down in the Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026.
The splashdown occurred after a 10-day mission around the Moon.
Artemis II is the first crewed mission to the lunar vicinity since 1972.
Artemis II focused on testing life support and safety.
Artemis II is the first crewed flight of NASA's Artemis program.
The Artemis II crew consisted of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
During the mission, the crew performed a “first return correction burn”.
During the mission, the crew tested the spacecraft's systems for future Mars missions.
The spacecraft successfully completed a “skip” entry into the Earth's atmosphere.
The spacecraft endured temperatures of 2,760°C before landing.
The spacecraft landed near San Diego.
In some contexts, "Integrity" is also used to refer to the Mission Control call sign during the mission.
